text:
maria: FYI — customer on Dedicated sees RuntimeError: This event loop is already running when calling the Python SDK inside a FastAPI endpoint. Works fine in a standalone script.

kai: Can you paste the traceback + minimal repro? Also which redwood sdk and httpx versions?

maria: Paste from customer: 
```
# app.py
from fastapi import FastAPI
from redwood import Client  # using sync client wrapper
app = FastAPI()
client = Client()

@app.get('/gen')
def gen():
    r = client.generate('summarize: ...')
    return {'out': r.text}

# traceback
RuntimeError: This event loop is already running
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/redwood/sync.py", line 40, in wrapper
    return asyncio.run(async_fn(*args, **kwargs))
```

customer says: python 3.10, uvicorn 0.18, redwood-sdk 0.3.7, httpx 0.23.3

eshan: This is the classic nested event loop issue — the sync wrapper uses asyncio.run which fails inside an already-running loop (uvicorn/ASGI). I can reproduce locally by calling the sync API from an async server.

kai: Confirmed. Quick guidance we should give the customer: 1) Use the async client API inside async endpoints (preferred). 2) If they must use sync API, run it in a threadpool so it doesn't call asyncio.run from the main loop. 3) Create a long-lived AsyncClient at app startup instead of per-request.

maria: Sending quick repro + two immediate fixes. Example 1 (preferred) — DI with async client at startup: 
```
from fastapi import FastAPI
from redwood import AsyncClient

app = FastAPI()
client = None

@app.on_event('startup')
async def startup_event():
    global client
    client = AsyncClient()
    await client.__aenter__()  # keep open across requests

@app.on_event('shutdown')
async def shutdown_event():
    await client.__aexit__(None, None, None)

@app.get('/gen')
async def gen():
    resp = await client.generate('summarize: ...')
    return {'out': resp.text}
```

Example 2 (sync wrapper workaround) — run sync call in thread: 
```
from anyio import to_thread
from redwood import Client  # sync client
client = Client()

@app.get('/gen')
async def gen():
    out = await to_thread.run_sync(lambda: client.generate('...'))
    return {'out': out.text}
```

eshan: Also note that creating/closing a client per-request is expensive and can cause connection churn/latency. Recommend single client per process and reusing it.

kai: I dug into SDK code: sync wrapper calls asyncio.run(...) which will always error if loop already running. Two actionable items for us: 1) short-term: update docs and support KB with the above patterns and explicit error message guiding the user. 2) medium-term: have SDK detect running loop and raise a clearer error that directs to async usage or thread workaround, or provide a helper like Client.from_sync_in_async() that internally uses to_thread.

maria: Customer asked if this could cause billing spikes because of retries — if they retry on failure at higher layers then yes, you can get duplicate requests. We advised them to add idempotency keys at application layer and disable automatic SDK retries until they switch to async-safe pattern.

support-bot: Created support ticket SUP-2025 with labels: python-sdk, event-loop, urgent. Assigned to eng-devex.

eshan: I opened a small reproducer repo and a unit test; can push PR to add a runtime check in sync wrapper to detect running loop and raise guidance. Planning to target patch 0.3.8.

kai: Customer follow-up: they upgraded to redwood-sdk 0.4.1 and switched endpoints to async client, confirmed the endpoint is now stable and latency dropped by ~20ms. :thumbsup:

maria: Marking resolved for now. If they see new traces, ask for full server logs, uvicorn worker config, and whether they use threads/gunicorn.

support-bot: Closing thread in 48h if no reply.
